scope: Read-only diagnosis of the T57 authenticated membership RPC on the frozen artifact's configured self-hosted Supabase origin; no fixture, product, database, auth, or deployment mutation
origin: The frozen 0.2.407 artifact and local .env.production both target db.matrxserver.com (see t57-artifact-origin-diagnosis-20261008.json). The connected Supabase MCP lists cloud projects, so the self-hosted live catalog was read through ai-matrx's existing public.execute_admin_query operator, with no user or membership rows selected through that privileged path.

live_catalog.result: TABLE(id uuid, organization_id uuid, container_id uuid, user_id uuid, role text, status text, created_at timestamptz)
live_catalog.exposure: authenticator pgrst.db_schemas begins api,public and includes iam; public is exposed but is not the default profile
live_catalog.permissions: authenticated has USAGE on public and EXECUTE on the function; anon lacks EXECUTE
live_catalog.placement: Only the public signature exists in pg_proc on the self-hosted origin; the database-estate-reduction plan's future iam.mbr_for_user placement is not live.

discriminating_probe: Using the existing aidream admin@admin.com test credential privately and the extension production publishable key, POST /rest/v1/rpc/mbr_for_user with p_container_type=organization and both Content-Profile: public and Accept-Profile: public returned HTTP 200 with 157 active membership rows. No token, organization ID, name, or row contents were printed or saved. The prior default and iam-profile PGRST202 probes addressed the wrong profiles; they do not indicate a missing function or failed membership.
client_path: src/lib/supabase/client.ts creates the ordinary client without a db override; installed supabase-js DEFAULT_DB_OPTIONS.schema is public and postgrest-js sends the schema profile. src/lib/org/active-org.ts invokes the plain-client mbr_for_user RPC and then reads iam.organizations by returned membership IDs. scripts/release-with-gate-auth.mjs independently encodes the same explicit public-profile membership call.
selected_label_explanation: The frozen resolver validates live membership, then selects device choice, account last active, account start-up, or first active membership. A ladder result is cached with viaLadder and does not write matrx.org.active. useActiveOrganization renders that resolved organization's name in Settings. Therefore T57's observed selected label with absent device storage is consistent with a successful public-profile membership read; the prior raw probe's PGRST202 was a separate request. The label alone still does not prove which UUID a later request used.
root_cause: The diagnostic RPC used the wrong PostgREST profile. The remaining T57 checkpoint failure is the native driver's storage-only assertion after it skipped an explicit switch because the approved label was already selected; this assertion rejects a valid account/start-up/first-membership ladder selection (see t57-organization-contract-20261008.json).
approved_fixture_verification: The existing mode-0600 test-results/admin-profile-approved-organization-private.json supplied the approved exact name. The same admin@admin.com authenticated session read public.mbr_for_user, then iam.organizations restricted to returned active membership IDs and archived_at IS NULL. Exactly one organization matched the approved name; its current membership UUID was written only into that same private fixture as approved_organization_id, preserving mode 0600. No name, UUID, membership row, or credential was printed or committed.
exact_repair_path: The private T57 fixture now has the uniquely matched current membership UUID. Update the native checkpoint to accept the ladder selection without device storage only when the approved visible name and current membership UUID agree, and capture a real product request's X-Organization-Id equal to that UUID. Preserve wrong-org/missing-org refusals; do not inject the header or infer an ID from the label.
claim_limit: The canonical RPC is deployed and readable for the admin fixture, and the approved T57 private fixture now carries a unique current active membership UUID. This lane did not capture a product X-Organization-Id and does not claim T57 acceptance.
